purpose: Measure household economic pressure by separating persistent essential need from delivered cost, disposable income, observed quantity acquired, and substitution/compression behavior. CPI is supporting evidence only and is not the governing welfare metric.
governing_principles: Underlying essential need or demand must not be inferred downward merely because observed quantity purchased or consumed declines.
Contracted commodity price and delivered total cost are distinct variables; mandatory delivery, transmission, distribution, taxes, riders, and surcharges remain visible.
Price index, dollar expenditure, units purchased, physical volume or weight, package size, calories or nutritional quantity, and household income are distinct state variables.

A household can spend the same or more dollars while acquiring less physical quantity; this is consistent with purchasing-power compression and must not be labeled demand destruction without separate evidence.
Higher cost in one essential category can reduce the ability to satisfy another essential need even when the second category's own price is unchanged.
National aggregates cannot be promoted to universal household or state-level findings without distributional evidence.

observations.notable_current_dollar_PCE_change: Gasoline and other energy goods accounted for $81.3 billion SAAR of the $195.4 billion monthly PCE increase; food and beverages accounted for $6.9 billion SAAR.
observations.interpretation: Nominal after-tax income rose while real after-tax purchasing power declined slightly; spending increased faster than real purchasing capacity.
Real disposable purchasing power contracted while current-dollar spending still increased and the saving rate fell.

food_quantity_anchor.interpretive_role: Observed retail unit acquisition is a closer quantity signal than dollars spent but remains incomplete without package-size-adjusted weight, volume, calories, and quality mix.

evaluation_rule: For each essential lane, reconstruct resources -> mandatory delivered cost -> dollars spent -> quantity or service acquired -> substitution/compression. Do not infer welfare improvement from a price-index decline alone, and do not infer lower underlying need from lower observed quantity alone.
cross_lane_rule: If one essential's delivered cost rises and another essential's quantity acquired falls, record the temporal relationship but do not infer cross-category causation unless income/budget or other independent evidence establishes the constraint path.
anti_hindsight_rules: Do not select a household burden metric after observing which one gives the strongest result; preserve every predeclared lane and its null or contradictory evidence.
Do not substitute annual, monthly, household, national, price, expenditure, or quantity measures for one another after observing outcomes.
Do not convert a national average into a universal household finding.
Do not treat correlation between diesel, freight, utility, or food costs as sole or dominant causation.
current_bounded_finding: March-April 2026 national macro evidence shows real disposable personal income declined in both months while current-dollar consumer outlays increased. Combined with independently preserved food unit-versus-dollar evidence, this supports an aggregate purchasing-power-compression lane and justifies evaluating essential delivered costs directly rather than using CPI as a household-welfare proxy.
